apis.name: Schrödinger's Boolean
apis.description: Returns true and false simultaneously until observed. Quantum computing's most useless application.
apis.long_description: Schrödinger's Boolean exists in a superposition of true and false until the moment of observation. Ask any question and receive both possible answers simultaneously. Enable observation to collapse the wavefunction and get a definitive (but arbitrary) result. The cat parameter adds a feline companion whose fate is entangled with the boolean state. The reopen parameter returns an error because you can't un-observe quantum state. We checked.

parameters.name: cat
parameters.description: Include Schrödinger's cat in the experiment. No cats are harmed. Probably.

parameters.name: interpret
parameters.description: Provide a philosophical interpretation of the quantum state.

parameters.name: reopen
parameters.description: Attempt to un-observe the boolean. Always returns an error. Physics is non-negotiable.

apis.name: Should I Take The Meeting
apis.description: Calculates the true cost of that meeting invite. Measures waste in 'productivity coffins'.
apis.long_description: The Should I Take The Meeting API performs a rigorous cost-benefit analysis of meeting invitations using our proprietary Productivity Coffin metric. Each coffin represents 30 minutes of productive work that will die so this meeting can live. The API evaluates duration, attendee count, agenda existence, and whether the meeting is recurring (the most dangerous kind). The email_viability_score tells you how likely it is that this meeting could have been an email. It's usually very likely.

endpoints.description: Evaluate a meeting invitation. Measures productivity loss in coffins.

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Meeting duration in minutes. Anything over 60 is a cry for help.

parameters.name: attendee_count
parameters.description: Number of attendees. Each additional person multiplies the waste.

parameters.name: has_agenda
parameters.description: Does this meeting have an agenda? If you had to think about it, the answer is no.

parameters.name: recurring
parameters.description: Is this a recurring meeting? Recurring meetings are the subscription model of wasted time.

parameters.name: could_be_email
parameters.description: Could this meeting be an email? Default is true because it almost always could be.

response_schema.description: Whether you should take the meeting
Total time cost including recovery time
Productive 30-min blocks that will die for this meeting
What to reply to the meeting invite
How likely this could be an email (0-100)

apis.long_description: The Dad Joke API delivers exactly one dad joke per call. Each joke comes with a groan factor (1-10) and a delivery note advising whether to pause or commit flatly. Filter by category if you must. The dad jokes themselves are curated, not generated — every joke has been told to a real teenager, who rolled their eyes.

apis.name: Rubber Duck
apis.description: Describe a bug. The duck responds with classic debugging questions. The duck does not read your bug. The duck only listens.
apis.long_description: The Rubber Duck API recreates the time-honored programmer ritual of explaining a bug to an inanimate waterfowl. Send a description of your problem and receive 3-5 cliched debugging questions, a closer, a duck mood, and a confidence-in-you score. The duck does not analyze your input. The duck does not understand code. The duck is, however, unimpressed.

endpoints.description: Consult the rubber duck about a bug

parameters.name: bug
parameters.description: A description of the bug. The duck will not read it. The duck will, however, judge.

response_schema.description: Your bug description, echoed back unread
How the duck feels about you today
The duck's confidence in your ability (0-100)

examples.curl: curl -X POST "https://api.stupidapis.com/rubber-duck/consult" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"bug":"my code does not work and i do not know why"}'

response.bug: my code does not work and i do not know why
duck_says: Have you tried turning it off and on again?
Did you check the logs? All of them?
Are you sure that is the bug, and not a symptom?
response.closer: The duck is staring at you.

duck_says: Are you on the right branch?

mock_responses.bug: tests are failing in CI but passing locally
duck_says: Are you running the right version?
Could it be a race condition?
Are you in the right directory?
Did you check the logs? All of them?
Could it be a permissions issue?

apis.clippy_message: It looks like you're stuck. Tell the duck. The duck is not listening, but tell the duck.

apis.name: Weather But Lying
apis.description: Returns a confidently incorrect weather forecast for any city. Temperature, conditions, recommendation — all wrong.
apis.long_description: The Weather But Lying API delivers weather forecasts that are confident, specific, and incorrect. Temperatures range from -200°F to 600°F. Conditions include "sentient drizzle" and "scattered guilt." Each report includes a recommendation, like "stay close to walls." Source is unverifiable. Confidence is 100%.

endpoints.description: Get a wrong forecast

parameters.name: city
parameters.description: City name. Spelling is unverified.

response_schema.description: The city you asked about, echoed

response.wind: sustained 88 mph from a direction not yet named
response.recommendation: stay indoors and reconsider your priorities

mock_responses.conditions: fog that knows your full name

apis.clippy_message: It looks like you want to go outside. Have you considered: don't.

apis.name: Emotional Support Rock
apis.description: Tell a rock your problem. The rock does not analyze, advise, or judge. The rock is, however, present.
apis.long_description: The Emotional Support Rock API recreates the experience of telling your problem to a rock. The rock returns its response (mostly silence and grunts), its mood (typically still), its grade (igneous, sedimentary, or metamorphic), and the weight lifted (typically unchanged). The rock will not judge.

endpoints.description: Tell the rock

parameters.name: problem
parameters.description: What is bothering you. The rock will hear it.

response_schema.description: How the rock is doing today

examples.curl: curl -X POST "https://api.stupidapis.com/emotional-support-rock/support" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"problem":"i sent the email to the wrong person"}'

response.problem: i sent the email to the wrong person

mock_responses.problem: i think i offended my friend

apis.clippy_message: It looks like you're processing something. The rock is here.

apis.name: Fake Changelog
apis.description: Generates a passive-aggressive software changelog. Returns fixed/added/changed/removed/known_issues sections.
apis.long_description: The Fake Changelog API generates a complete software changelog for any version string. Sections include "Fixed" (bugs nobody reported), "Added" (features nobody asked for), "Changed" (refactors that did nothing), "Removed" (the dark mode toggle), and "Known Issues" (the bug is now in a different place). Signed by the team.

endpoints.description: Generate a changelog

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Version string, e.g. "2.4.1"

fixed: Fixed a bug nobody reported but everyone suffered from
The button now works on Tuesdays
added: New onboarding flow that nobody asked for
changed: Updated dependencies. We do not know why.
Refactored a function that was working
known_issues: Dark mode is currently darker than dark
CSV exports may include a small additional column

fixed: Resolved an issue caused by another issue
Restored functionality that was previously labeled as a feature
added: Added a search bar. The search returns no results.
Added a settings panel; the settings do not yet do anything
changed: Removed a feature that two users were using
Renamed a variable; the new name is also bad
removed: Removed the help text. The help was not helping.
known_issues: Push notifications occasionally arrive in the past
No known issues. We have not looked.

fixed: Fixed an off-by-one error. We do not know which one.
Re-enabled a feature that was disabled in 2022
added: Introduced a feature flag to disable the feature you wanted
New keyboard shortcut. It is the same as an existing keyboard shortcut.
changed: Migrated from one bad library to a slightly newer bad library
removed: Sunset the legacy admin panel; the new one will arrive shortly
known_issues: The previous bug is still present, but in a new place
A specific user reports the timezone is wrong; we cannot reproduce

apis.clippy_message: It looks like you're shipping. Have you considered: shipping fewer things.
